explain.say: In 1798 a small book appeared in Bristol with no author's name on it: Lyrical Ballads. Inside were poems by two young friends, William Wordsworth and Samuel Taylor Coleridge. Many date English Romanticism from that book. The timeline follows Wordsworth's long life.

explain.say: What was new? On the left, the poetry of the 1700s, with fancy poetic diction about polite society. On the right, Wordsworth's Preface of 1800: poems in the language really used by men, about humble country lives. Poetry, he said, is the spontaneous overflow of powerful feelings. Do you agree?

explain.say: The friends split the work. Coleridge would make the supernatural feel real, as in the Ancient Mariner. Wordsworth would make ordinary life feel wonderful, as in a child's poem, We Are Seven. Look at the sort. Which half sounds more exciting?

explain.say: Here is how Wordsworth said a poem is made. Follow the chain: a powerful feeling, like daffodils dancing by a lake; time passes; then, lying calm on his couch, the feeling returns and flashes upon that inward eye. He called it emotion recollected in tranquillity. Has a memory ever hit you like that?

explain.say: The book ended with Tintern Abbey, a poem about memory and nature. Later the young rebel became Poet Laureate, and critics like Jerome McGann asked whether Romantic nature was an escape from politics. Lovely work. Challenge: write four plain lines about a place you remember.

faq.a: A collection of poems by Wordsworth and Coleridge, published anonymously in 1798, that used plain language and ordinary subjects and is often seen as the start of English Romanticism.

faq.q: What did Wordsworth say poetry is?
faq.a: In the 1800 Preface he called good poetry the spontaneous overflow of powerful feelings, and said it takes its origin from emotion recollected in tranquillity.

faq.q: Why did Wordsworth use ordinary language?
faq.a: He believed the speech of rural people was purer and closer to real feeling than the artificial poetic diction of the 1700s, and that poetry should speak to everyone.

faq.q: How did Wordsworth and Coleridge divide the work?
faq.a: Coleridge later explained in Biographia Literaria (1817) that he would make supernatural subjects feel real, while Wordsworth would give ordinary life the charm of novelty.
asks: Who wrote what in Lyrical Ballads?

faq.q: What is emotion recollected in tranquillity?
faq.a: Wordsworth's idea that a poem begins when a strong feeling is remembered later in calm, until the feeling returns and flows into words, as in his daffodils poem.

facts: Lyrical Ballads was first published anonymously in Bristol in 1798.
The famous Preface appeared in the second edition of 1800.
The Prelude was published in 1850, after Wordsworth's death.
